title: Variant Showcase: Runway Evaluation and Decision Memo (Jul 2027)
content:
Purpose:
This memo summarizes a short, focused comparative evaluation run ("Runway") for three candidate model variants for the domain-conditioned summarization workload used by the knowledge products team. The goal is to pick a candidate to promote into the onboarding shadow fleet for a 2-week production shadow, or to reject and continue iteration.

Quick verdict (tl;dr):
- Nominate: redwood-v2-alpha-small-quant ("Alpha-Q") as the primary candidate for a 2-week shadow rollout. It offers a consistent cost/latency improvement with acceptable regression risk on the most sensitive prompt cohort.
- Rationale: Alpha-Q shows +5-7% median improvement on latency and a 20–35% reduction in per-token cost versus the current baseline, while winning on usability-sensitive metrics for the majority of prompt cohorts. There are concentrated regressions on a narrow legal-template cohort; we propose targeted prompt-set augmentation and a canary guard before full promotion.

Experiment scope and constraints:
- Date range: 2027-07-08 → 2027-07-14 (7 days).
- Environment: internal eval harness (v0.9.3), micro-batch=8, KV cache warmed per session, stable infra (p99 infra variance <2%).
- Workload: 3,200 holdout prompts derived from product logs (last 90 days), stratified into cohorts: general-info, long-doc (>4k tokens), legal-templates, multi-turn-chats, and headline-summaries.
- Metrics captured: ROUGE-L, ROUGE-1, BERTScore, human-preference A/B (pairwise sampled, n=600), latency p50/p95, cost-per-1k-tokens (estimate using current pricing model), and regression signal index (RSI) computed per-prompt relative to baseline.
- Baseline: redwood-v1-std ("Baseline"). Candidates: redwood-v2-alpha-small-quant ("Alpha-Q"), redwood-v2-alpha-fp16 ("Alpha-F"), third-party llama-13b-slim ("L13-Slim").

Prompt sets and known sensitivities:
- Promptset A (general-info): short, open questions. Sensitive to hallucination.
- Promptset B (long-doc): multi-paragraph summarization with explicit instructions. Sensitive to context-window handling and KV-cache correctness.
- Promptset C (legal-templates): short-forms where phrase precision matters. Sensitive to minor tokenization/phrase shifts.
- Promptset D (multi-turn): chat-like history with instructions. Sensitive to instruction-following and model drift.
- Promptset E (headlines): brevity and creativity tradeoffs.

Leaderboard (aggregate metrics, higher is better unless noted):
- Columns: Model | ROUGE-L (mean) | BERTScore (mean) | Human-pref % (vs baseline) | Latency p50 (ms) | Cost per 1k tokens (relative)
- Baseline (redwood-v1-std): 0.412 | 0.872 | 50% | 175 ms | 1.00x
- Alpha-F (v2 fp16): 0.418 | 0.877 | 56% | 140 ms | 0.92x
- Alpha-Q (v2 small quant): 0.410 | 0.869 | 60% | 120 ms | 0.70x
- L13-Slim: 0.400 | 0.860 | 40% | 210 ms | 0.95x

Notes on leaderboard:
- Alpha-Q shows slightly lower ROUGE-L relative to Alpha-F (−0.8 pts) but wins the human-preference tests at sample size with p<0.05 (A/B against baseline). The human pref gains come primarily from Promptsets A and E (general and headline tasks) where brevity and concise phrasing are favored.
- Alpha-F is a safe accuracy win by automatic metrics but offers less cost savings.

Win/Loss summary (pairwise against Baseline, aggregated counts across 3,200 prompts):
- Alpha-Q: Wins 1,960 | Losses 980 | Ties 260 (win rate 61%)
- Alpha-F: Wins 1,720 | Losses 1,120 | Ties 360 (win rate 54%)
- L13-Slim: Wins 1,120 | Losses 1,800 | Ties 280 (win rate 35%)

Cohort breakdown (high level):
- General-info (900 prompts): Alpha-Q win rate 68%, Alpha-F 62%, L13-Slim 40%.
- Long-doc (600 prompts): Alpha-F edges out (win rate 58%) — Alpha-Q suffers slight context fidelity issues in specific long-chain references.
- Legal-templates (400 prompts): Alpha-Q loses (win rate 32%) with frequent token-level substitution errors (dates/numbers formatting) that lower ROUGE and human pref. Alpha-F matches baseline.
- Multi-turn (800 prompts): Alpha-Q and Alpha-F comparable (~55% each), both better than L13-Slim.
- Headlines (500 prompts): Alpha-Q strong (72% win rate).

Qualitative triage notes (sourced from 200 human annotations):
- Alpha-Q: tends to favor shorter, clearer summaries; occasionally truncates crucial qualifiers in legal-template outputs. The truncations are deterministic and correlate with a quantized attention scaling artifact in long, precise sequences.
- Alpha-F: higher fidelity in long-docs; answers are slightly more verbose which helps in legal templates but costs tokens.
- L13-Slim: inconsistent instruction following; creative hallucinations in headlines.

Statistical checks and caveats:
- Human-pref A/B used stratified sampling and bootstrap CI; Alpha-Q vs Baseline: 60% (95% CI 56–64%), p=0.012.
- For legal-template cohort, absolute differences are small numerically but sensitive in product; downstream error cost high.
- Infrastructure variability was monitored; no confounding incidents recorded.

Decision and recommended plan:
1) Shadow rollout candidate: Alpha-Q into a 2-week shadow fleet for the knowledge-products customer segment only (5% of traffic), with logging hooks and exact-match alerting on legal-template prompts.
2) Prep work before shadow start (owners and deadlines):
   - Prompt augmentation: curate +150 legal-template prompts (Sofia) — due 2027-07-25. Add to targeted RLHF-like weighting in fine-tune recipe or instruct prompt templates.
   - Canary guard: add exact-match regression-alert on legal-template RSI > 0.06 (Arjun) — due 2027-07-22.
   - Monitoring: add cohort dashboards (latency, RSI, human-pref sample) and attach automatic rollback trigger if legal-template human pref drops >10% at day-7 (Liam) — due 2027-07-24.
3) If Shadow outcomes after 2 weeks show:
   - No material regressions (legal-template < 5% worse and human pref stable): schedule staged promotion to shadow-50% across multiple customer segments with a rollback window.
   - Persistent regressions: pause promotion and run a targeted micro-fine-tune on 2–4k legal-template examples, then re-eval.

Rollback and safety posture:
- Immediate fallback path: route affected prompts to Alpha-F (v2 fp16) when RSI alarm fires — this keeps accuracy while trading some cost.
- Configured automated fallback in routing policy and ensure traceable traces for every fallback decision.

Open questions and unknowns:
- Is the quantization artifact in Alpha-Q fixed by a revised kernel selection (we suspect yes) or requires re-quantization? (Owner: eng-serving-runtime, blocked until infra bench complete).
- Acceptable product-level tolerance for legal-template micro-regressions — product to quantify business impact (owner: knowledge-products PM).

Appendix (short):
- Full raw leaderboard CSV: linked in Confluence (ML-ONBOARD-672).
- Sampling details: human A/B protocol and marking rubric included in linked artifacts.
- Experiment run IDs: run_2027_07_08_rv2_alpha_q, run_2027_07_09_rv2_alpha_fp16, run_2027_07_10_llama13_slim.

Action items summary (owner — deliverable — due):
- Sofia Reyes — legal-template prompt augmentation (+150) — 2027-07-25.
- Arjun Patel — implement RSI canary alert + fallback route — 2027-07-22.
- Liam O'Connor — cohort dashboards + rollout gating automation — 2027-07-24.
- Maya Chen — schedule shadow deployment window and coordinate with infra — 2027-07-21.

Comments / next sync:
- Quick sync proposed 2027-07-21 to confirm readiness for shadow (15 min). Please review this memo and add objections/comments inline in Confluence ML-ONBOARD-672 before 2027-07-20 EOD.

End of memo.
